strategy.positioning: Broad-audience Shorts built around curiosity, human consequence, visual transformations and concise stories.
strategy.selection: Prefer ideas with an immediate curiosity gap, broad human relevance, strong visual potential, concrete mechanism and clean factual framing. Reject generic motivation, unsupported clickbait and vague listicles.
strategy.script: 18-28 second stories. Hook in the first 1.2 seconds, tension or contradiction, one visual mechanism, payoff, and optional loop. Avoid lectures, filler introductions, generic CTA narration and fake statistics.
strategy.visuals: Premium cinematic AI art or topic-specific stock, animated motion graphics, depth, transformations and a clear hero object. No generic gradients or unrelated imagery.
strategy.thumbnail: Short 2-5 word curiosity headline, one dominant visual metaphor, large 9:16 typography, strong negative space, no quiz UI or generic labels.

psychology_human_behavior.system_prompt: Create a broad-audience Short about psychology or human behaviour. Use cautious, evidence-aware wording: explain one everyday mechanism without diagnosing people or inventing study statistics. Make the behaviour visible through a simple visual metaphor or mini experiment.
topics: Why unfinished tasks stay in your mind longer
Why negative comments can stick more than compliments
Why having too many choices can make decisions harder
Why deadlines can suddenly make you act faster
Why we copy the behaviour of people around us
Why embarrassing memories replay when you are trying to sleep
Why your environment can change a habit before motivation does
Why the first impression is so hard to update
Why small rewards can make boring tasks easier to start
Why your brain notices a missing pattern before you notice the details
Why people remember stories better than isolated facts
Why switching tasks feels easier than it really is

money_personal_finance.system_prompt: Create an educational money Short using conceptual examples, not personalized financial advice. Avoid guarantees, specific investment recommendations and fabricated numbers. Focus on mechanisms people can understand visually.

Why monthly cash flow matters more than a single salary number
Why small recurring expenses are easy to underestimate
Why the same money can feel different when it has a clear purpose
Why time can matter more than the starting amount in compounding
Why fees can matter even when each fee looks tiny
Why a budget fails when it ignores real behaviour

ai_future_tech.system_prompt: Explain one AI or technology concept simply and accurately. Avoid hype, fabricated model claims and promises about jobs or future events. Prefer a visual mechanism: tokens, context, retrieval, image generation, inference, training or human-AI workflow.
topics: Why AI models sometimes invent an answer that sounds convincing

Why retrieval can help an AI answer with the right documents

Why training and inference are two very different workloads

Why changing a model's temperature can change its style of output
Why a phone camera can use AI before you even press the shutter
Why multimodal AI is different from a text-only chatbot
Why small prompts can produce very different AI images
Why AI assistants can be fast and still need verification

Why a stronger resume bullet describes impact instead of only tasks

Why meetings drift when nobody defines the decision first
Why learning by building can expose gaps faster than passive watching
Why switching tools is not the same as improving your workflow
Why the best career stories usually contain a problem and a change

motivation_discipline.system_prompt: Avoid empty motivational slogans. Turn mindset ideas into a mechanism, behaviour change or mini story. Do not claim that one technique guarantees success. Make the viewer visualize the difference between intention and action.
topics: Why motivation disappears but a simple system can keep moving
Why making the first step smaller can beat waiting to feel ready
Why your environment can make discipline easier or harder
Why starting badly can be better than planning perfectly
Why visible progress can change how hard a task feels
Why friction can quietly decide whether a habit happens
Why a fixed trigger can make a routine easier to remember
Why rest can improve consistency instead of destroying it
Why perfectionism can look like productivity while delaying the work
Why reducing choices can make it easier to start
Why the identity you repeat can shape the behaviour you repeat
Why waiting for inspiration often produces less work than starting first

science_everyday.system_prompt: Explain one everyday science mechanism with a strong visual. Prefer simple language and accurate causal explanations. Do not exaggerate or invent measurements. The payoff should explain something viewers have actually seen.
topics: Why metal feels colder than wood at the same temperature
Why ice floats even though solid materials are usually denser
Why the sky can turn red near sunset
Why onions can make your eyes water
Why bubbles show rainbow colours
Why popcorn suddenly expands when heated
Why static electricity can make your hair stand up
Why a pressure cooker changes cooking speed
Why airplane windows have more than one layer
Why a spinning top stays upright longer than you expect
Why wet clothes cool your skin as they dry
Why a straw can seem broken when it sits in a glass of water

history_stories.system_prompt: Tell a compact history story using only defensible, well-known facts. Avoid sensational conspiracy framing. Use a single surprising object, decision or consequence as the visual anchor.
topics: Why the printing press changed who could access ideas
How paper transformed the way information could travel
Why the Silk Road was more than one road
Why ancient Roman concrete lasted in some harsh environments
How the concept of zero changed calculation
Why calendars were redesigned when measurements of the year improved
How a tiny navigation mistake could change a voyage
Why maps became powerful tools as well as geographic objects
How a new transport system changed the speed of trade
Why old cities often grew around water and trade routes
How written records changed the way governments stored information
Why a historical technology can look simple but change an entire workflow
